sam: quick heads-up — ran the micro-handshake window split on pool-d3 this morning. overall throughput steady but P99 on short prefill->decode flows (<=32 tokens) spiked.

sam: repro steps: 1) baseline warm KV, 2) run 10k short chat requests (prompt ~20 tokens, gen ~8), 3) compare latencies. patch: stagger prefill handshake window by phase and bias kernel selection toward kernel-A for prefill.

sam: raw numbers (local microbench): baseline decode P99 = 142ms, patch decode P99 = 210ms; prefill P50 improved 5ms. tail moved a lot for decode.

alex: do you have kernel selection and batch-size hist? does kernel-A explain the tail?

sam: yes — kernel logs show kernel-A used much more often for prefill after biasing. snippet:
```
[2026-03-19T09:12:03Z] select_kernel(prefill, bs=2) -> kernel-A (78%)
[2026-03-19T09:12:03Z] select_kernel(decode, bs=2) -> kernel-B (60%)
```
Kernel-A seems to have higher variance for tiny batch shapes (bs<=4) on this device.

maria: batch hist post-patch:
- 1-2 tokens: 46%
- 3-8 tokens: 32%
- >8 tokens: 22%
Baseline 1-2 tokens was ~28% (so way more tiny batches now). also KV hit rate dropped ~4% (KV priming delayed because prefill windows occasionally wait and let gen steal cache warmups).

kevin: interesting — looks like queue ordering changed and allowed more init-gen style tiny flows through earlier. quick experiments to try:
- reduce prefill backoff from 8ms -> 2ms
- add kernel-affinity override: if bs<=4 then prefer kernel-B
- bump token_budget floor for short flows so we ensure coalescing

bench-bot: perf-regression-suite ran: 5812345678-microhandshake-run -> artifacts uploaded (s3://redwood-tests/5812345678/)

alex: +1 to kernel-affinity. if kernel-A gives worse tail for tiny batches, force kernel-B fallback for bs<=4; we can measure perf delta and then relax.

sam: I'll apply the three tweaks on a canary and re-run the microbench. plan: canary -> 1h soak -> full pool. If P99 doesn't improve I will revert the handshake-split. posting results in ~2 hours. thanks :thumbsup:
